title: Lattice paths around a few blocks
statement: Count right/down paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of an m × n grid (m, n ≤ 10⁵) that avoid every blocked cell (at most 300 of them), mod 10⁹+7.
hints: The grid DP has 10¹⁰ cells: impossible. With no blocks the answer is C(m + n − 2, m − 1).
Sort the blocked cells; ways[i] = paths to block i avoiding all earlier blocks = C(to i) − Σ ways[j]·C(j → i).

solution.explanation: The grid DP from Part 6 is O(mn), hopeless here. Combinatorics replaces it: free paths are binomial coefficients, and blocks are handled by inclusion–exclusion over the first block hit. Sorting makes every earlier block a possible predecessor; ways[i] counts paths reaching block i with no block before it. The target is treated as the last "block". Cost depends on the number of blocks, not the grid area.
solution.python:
def count_paths(m, n, blocked):
    M = 10**9 + 7
    N = m + n
    f = [1] * (N + 1)
    for i in range(1, N + 1):
        f[i] = f[i - 1] * i % M
    inv = [1] * (N + 1)
    inv[N] = pow(f[N], M - 2, M)
    for i in range(N, 0, -1):
        inv[i - 1] = inv[i] * i % M
    C = lambda a, b: f[a] * inv[b] % M * inv[a - b] % M if 0 <= b <= a else 0
    pts = sorted(tuple(p) for p in blocked) + [(m - 1, n - 1)]
    ways = []
    for i, (r, c) in enumerate(pts):
        w = C(r + c, r)
        for j in range(i):
            pr, pc = pts[j]
            if pr <= r and pc <= c:
                w = (w - ways[j] * C(r - pr + c - pc, r - pr)) % M
        ways.append(w)
    return ways[-1]
